question: Breaker trips immediately every time we close it. No relay targets, but the 86 lockout relay flag is still showing tripped.

report.likely_cause: The breaker trips immediately every time we close it.
steps: Check the closing mechanism and verify the lockout relay status.
Identify all sources (incl. backfeeds, UPS/battery, CT/VT secondaries, stored energy).
Wear PPE per the arc-flash/shock risk assessment while testing.
Verify absence of voltage with a rated meter (live-dead-live).

results.title: Circuit Breaker Trip and Close Circuit Troubleshooting / Breaker trips immediately on close
results.text: If a breaker trips as soon as it is closed, determine whether a protective relay operated. If relay targets show an instantaneous (50) or differential (87) trip, the breaker likely closed into a fault or a setting/CT issue exists (see protective relay basics). If no relay target is present, suspect the control scheme: a maintained trip signal (stuck relay contact, an 86 lockout that was not reset, a shorted control s...

results.title: Protective Relay Basics (ANSI Device Numbers) / Reading relay targets and event records
results.text: Before resetting anything, record the front-panel targets, the 86 lockout status, and download the event report. The event shows which element operated, the phases involved, the current and voltage magnitudes, and the timing. Do not repeatedly reset and re-close a breaker that tripped on a protective function without finding the cause.

results.title: Circuit Breaker Trip and Close Circuit Troubleshooting / Breaker fails to close
results.text: Causes include: closing spring not charged (failed charging motor, open motor fuse, or motor limit switch), an active 86 lockout or trip signal (trip-free), anti-pump relay sealed in, open close coil, low DC voltage, a racking or position interlock that is not satisfied, or a 52b contact problem in the close circuit. Check the spring-charged indicator and the close circuit voltage first.
